To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the WDF can be reconstructed from Talbot interference of large molecules and the reconstructed WDF exhibits quantum interference effects.

the WDF of large molecules can be reconstructed from de Broglie Talbot interference frings, that the WDF can be reconstructed in a partially coherent situation and that negativity in the partially reconstructed distribution can be observed.
the WDF of heavy molecules can be reconstructed from Talbot–Lauer interference experiments, and that the WDF can be partially reconstructed even in the presence of incoherent factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the motonic quantum state from the interference pattern of large molecules.
the reconstruction of the motonic quantum state of heavy particles from the near-field de Broglie wave interference.
a theoretical study of the Wigner function reconstruction of a motional quantum state in a de Broglie interferometer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can expect a reconstruction of the motonic quantum state of the molecule from the interference fringes, but the quality of the reconstruction is limited.

, in spite of the fact that the reconstruction of the quantum state in motion is not possible in the near-field case, the negativity of the WDF is a promising indicator for the wavelike nature of matter.
the WDF reconstruction from de Broglie diffraction is possible in the near-field, even if the experimental conditions are not optimal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to extract the WDF of a quantum superposition state from a near-field interference experiment.
the WDF can be reconstructed with a finite slit number, collimation, and particle-slit interaction in the near-field of the Talbot experiment.
it is possible to reconstruct a partially negative WDF in a Talbot–Laur interferometer for large molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reconstruction of the quantum state of a large molecule from the WDF is possible in a near-field experiment, even though the WDF is not reconstructed completely.
it is possible to extract the quantum state of a particle in motion from the WDF reconstructed from Talbot interference patterns.
a WDF reconstruction of the quantum state of matter-wave interferometry is feasible in principle.
